extracted.intended_audience: early-stage startup founders, people turning side projects into companies, and those curious about becoming founders
extracted.subtask_description: Information and participation guidance for Y Combinator's Startup School — a free, self-paced online course (plus optional in-person event) that teaches how to start a company, offers co‑founder matching, and provides weekly accountability tools. Targets founders at very early stages or those exploring founding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended audience / eligibility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "It's for anyone at the early stages of building a startup, turning a side project into a company, or anyone curious to learn about becoming a founder." Use this as the target participant profile when deciding whether to apply or enroll.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time commitment / pacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated duration and weekly time required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Go at your own pace. It will take approximately 7 weeks if you spend 1-2 hours/week." Treat ~1–2 hours per week over ~7 weeks as the recommended engagement level to complete the course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum / core topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary instructional modules and topics covered by the course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed sessions include: "How to Plan your MVP" (Michael Seibel), "Modern Startup Funding" (Carolynn Levy), "How to Launch your Company in the Press" (Kat Manalac), "How to Get Users and Grow" (Gustaf Alstromer), "How to Lead Teams" (Ali Rowghani), "How and When to Apply to Y Combinator" (Dalton Caldwell), plus founding stories and case studies (e.g., Mark Zuckerberg on Facebook, Anne Wojcicki on 23andMe). Use this list to judge topical fit for founders' needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor authority / provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Who teaches and credibility of content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course content is "taught by Y Combinator partners and industry leaders" and billed as coming from "the same people who helped Airbnb, Doordash, Stripe, Reddit, and Coinbase get started." Use instructor provenance as a quality signal when evaluating the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co‑founder matching workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: How the YC co‑founder matching platform works and what actions it expects from users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: "Create your profile" → "Let other founders know your preferences for interests, skills, location, and more" → "See potential co‑founders" (platform shows candidates best suited for you based on your requirements and preferences) → "Connect with your matches" (send invitations and explore working together). Also notes: "YC Co-Founder Matching: the world's largest co-founder matching platform, with over 100,000 matches made." Use these steps as the procedural rubric for using the matching service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability / progress tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: Tools for tracking startup progress while in the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page advertises "A weekly update tool to track your growth and progress." This implies an expectation of weekly self-reporting to maintain accountability; use the tool to measure and communicate progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost / access
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The course is described as "a free online course on how to start a startup." Use "free" as the access criterion; sign-up is required ("Sign up" / "Sign in").

rubrics_metrics.name: In‑person event application
rubrics_metrics.description: Application for attending Startup School 2026 in San Francisco.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page includes a call to action: "Looking to attend Startup School 2026 in San Francisco? Apply here for a spot." While no application criteria are provided on-page, this signals there is a separate application process for the in‑person component.
